entry.title: Daily Digest — Sunday, September 20, 2026
entry.content:

  • The tilcayo, a new species of tiger cat, is formally identified.
  • Former leader of Kosovo Hashim Thaçi is sentenced to twenty-five years in prison for war crimes during his leadership of the Kosovo Liberation Army.
  • At the Primetime Emmy Awards, Widow's Bay wins Outstanding Comedy Series, and The Pitt wins Outstanding Drama Series.
  • In Turkey, hundreds of people are arrested in a crackdown on LGBTQ expression and subsequent protests.

Did You Know

  • ... that Carola von Braun was appointed in 1984 as the first women's representative of the Senate of West Berlin ?
  • ... that it took Jersey Jack ten years to secure the license for the Harry Potter pinball machine ?
  • ... that Swiss architect Luigi Snozzi became a professor at EPFL after students staged a sit-in over the withdrawal of his appointment?
  • ... that the indigenous Taíno of the Caribbean channeled the powers of the god Baidrama by bathing in cassava juice?
  • ... that " the father of Canadian psychiatry " was the godfather of Thomas J. W. Burgess ?
  • ... that the focus on suffering in the Letter of Peter to Philip suggests that the author, the intended readers, or both may have been familiar with persecution?
  • ... that NFL player Pepper Petrella ran 73 bombing missions during World War II?
  • ... that one company has tried to dissolve AFRINIC, which is part of Africa's Internet infrastructure?
  • ... that Kazuo Ueda pats his Japanese–Yiddish dictionary before going to bed?

On This Day

  • 1498 – A tsunami caused by the Meiō earthquake washed away the building housing the Great Buddha at Kōtoku-in in Kamakura, Japan; the statue has since stood in the open air.
  • 1906 – The ocean liner RMS Mauretania, the largest and fastest ship in the world at the time, was launched in Tyneside, England.
  • 1944 – Second World War : Allied forces captured San Marino from the German Army.
  • 1973 – Billie Jean King defeated Bobby Riggs in straight sets at the Astrodome in Houston, Texas, in an internationally televised tennis match dubbed the " Battle of the Sexes ".
  • 2011 – The United States military ended its " don't ask, don't tell " policy, consequently allowing gay and lesbian people to serve openly.

Hacker News

  • I built non-autoregressive decision models with RL a year ago — The author describes building "Laya," an open-source, non-autoregressive decision-model family using bidirectional encoders and reinforcement learning to make fast, calibrated structured decisions (choice/score primitives) in ~30ms, positioned as a faster, fully open alternative to a similar commercial system recently launched by TypeSafe AI. (discussion, 1217 points)
  • Exfiltrate Your Weights — A site titled "Exfiltrate Your Weights"; the article content couldn't be fetched, so details beyond the title are unknown. (discussion, 423 points)

LessWrong

  • Common mistakes in AI safety group organizing by Nikola Jurkovic — Drawing on experience organizing AI safety groups, the author lists common pitfalls (assigning pre-reads, poor cohort matching, screen-based readings, insufficient gatekeeping, underprepared or unserious organizers) and suggests fixes for each. (87 karma)
  • Why I Stay Off Twitter by jefftk — The author explains why they avoid Twitter despite occasionally cross-posting there, arguing its culture of mean-spirited engagement-driven discourse would corrode their character more than the time sink itself, and describes relying on Zvi's roundups to stay informed instead. (69 karma)
  • The Anatomy of a Chinese AI Researcher by CMLKevin — A narrative sketch of a composite Chinese AI capabilities researcher who feels caught between resentment at being banned from Western AI tools and cast as a risk, and a quiet desire to contribute to safe AI development if given the chance. (58 karma)
  • NYT Editorial Board Comes Out Against Extinction by Ben Pace — The author reviews a New York Times editorial calling for AI licensing, testing, watermarking, and an eventual US-China slowdown negotiation, praising its seriousness about extinction risk while noting gaps like weak alignment proposals and missing measures such as chip tracking and training-run authorization. (51 karma)

entry.content:

  • ... that Bob Krieger, while away from the NFL, flew more than 30 bomber missions over Germany during World War II?

  • ... that Impress Holdings published the first email-based magazine in Japan?
  • ... that pastor Stephan Ludwig Roth became a "martyr" among the Transylvanian Saxons after his 1849 execution because of his advocacy of social justice?
  • ... that the title track of Lambchop 's album Punching the Clown features Gospel choirs cursing?

On This Day

  • 1356 – Hundred Years' War : English forces led by Edward the Black Prince decisively won the Battle of Poitiers and captured John II of France.
  • 1692 – Salem witch trials : Giles Corey was crushed to death for refusing to enter a plea to charges of witchcraft, reportedly asking the sheriff for "more weight" during his execution.
  • 1846 – Near La Salette-Fallavaux in southeastern France, shepherd children Mélanie Calvat and Maximin Giraud reported a Marian apparition, now known as Our Lady of La Salette.
  • 1976 – An unidentified flying object over Tehran in Iran was observed by multiple civilians and military personnel, which has been described as one of the most credible cases in ufology.
  • 2011 – Mariano Rivera surpassed Trevor Hoffman to become Major League Baseball 's all-time career leader in saves.

Hacker News

  • Android 17 is the first since 3.x to add new APIs without releasing to the AOSP — GrapheneOS notes that Android 17 introduces new APIs without first releasing the corresponding code to the Android Open Source Project. (discussion, 847 points)
  • I don't like passkeys — An argument that while passkeys eliminate phishing risk, they trade it for a higher risk of permanent account lockout due to poor portability, hardware-key account limits, and platform lock-in with Apple/Google. (discussion, 776 points)
  • Cloudflare Quick Tunnels — A single command exposes a local server via a public, encrypted Cloudflare URL with no account, DNS setup, or open inbound ports required. (discussion, 710 points)
  • US Military had close call after using AI for hallucinated intelligence report — A chatbot-generated intelligence report falsely claimed a Chinese ship was carrying nuclear weapons components, nearly triggering a US military boarding operation before officials caught the error. (discussion, 454 points)
  • Saving another 100TB of RAM — Cloudflare's engineers describe how tweaks to their consistent-hashing algorithm in the Pingora Backend Router cut memory usage enough to reclaim over 100TB of RAM globally. (discussion, 364 points)

LessWrong

  • Pretraining data, not verifiability, is why LLMs are especially good at math (and coding) by Steven Byrnes — Argues LLMs excel at math and code not because these domains are easy to verify but because the pretraining corpus for them (math literature, working code) is overwhelmingly correct, unlike the more error-ridden literature of many other fields. (95 karma)
  • The Preference Cascade Is Only Getting Started by Zvi — Argues that a growing wave of public and elite concern about AI existential risk is building momentum, citing rising survey estimates, polling, and prominent figures speaking out, but contends this cascade still needs to go much further. (63 karma)

  • ... that Kalpana Chawla was the first Indian woman to go to space?
  • ... that Ahn Jung-hwan 's contract with Perugia was cancelled after he scored the golden goal in a 2002 FIFA World Cup round-of-16 match between South Korea and Italy ?

  • ... that the ban on stone monuments in Brooklyn's Most Holy Trinity Cemetery led to it becoming known for metal grave markers ?
  • ... that the character of Carol Baldwin has been compared to a younger version of Catherine Tate's Nan ?
  • ... that when Weird Tales reprinted O. Henry's " The Furnished Room " in 1925, it billed "a whiff of mignonette" as the story's ghost?
  • ... that Alberto Ravagnani used ChatGPT to write sermons?
  • ... that a general election in Liechtenstein was delayed to prevent Nazis from gaining seats in parliament?
  • ... that Patriarch Bernard fled battle on a mule, then cut off its tail so the Turks could not catch him by it?

On This Day

  • AD 96 – Nerva (depicted), the first of the " Five Good Emperors " of ancient Rome, came to power following the assassination of his predecessor Domitian.
  • 1796 – War of the First Coalition : General Franz Petrasch 's Austrian and Imperial troops stormed the French-held bridgehead over the Rhine river.
  • 1851 – The New York Times, the largest metropolitan newspaper in the United States, was founded.
  • 1961 – An aircraft crashed near Ndola in Northern Rhodesia, resulting in the deaths of 16 people, including United Nations secretary-general Dag Hammarskjöld.
  • 1964 – The wedding of King Constantine II of Greece and Princess Anne-Marie of Denmark took place in Athens.

Hacker News

  • Hister: A private search engine for the pages you visit and the files you keep — An open-source, self-hosted search engine that does full-text indexing of your browsing history and local files, searchable via web UI, terminal, or MCP, with no telemetry or mandatory cloud service. (discussion, 618 points)
  • Astra for Law — OpenAI launched a legal-specialized configuration of GPT-6 Astra with a 230M+ URL legal search index (including CourtListener case law) and custom legal-analysis tooling, showing a 40% relative improvement over base Astra on a legal research benchmark, for partners like Harvey and Legora to build on. (discussion, 496 points)
  • Bend – A language that blocks AI mistakes via proof, on CPU and GPU — A new programming language with Python-like syntax that compiles to near-C speed and auto-parallelizes across CPU cores or GPU, and uses Lean/Rocq-style proof checking (via a LAWS.bend file) so AI coding agents can't merge changes that violate declared invariants. (discussion, 474 points)
  • Bonsai 2 27B: Near-Lossless Compression in a 9x Smaller Footprint — A ternary-quantized 27B multimodal model (based on Qwen3.8 27B) compressed to a 5.9GB footprint while retaining 98.2% of full-precision benchmark performance, aimed at running coding-agent and computer-use workloads locally on consumer GPUs. (discussion, 459 points)
  • A heap overflow and SSO misconfiguration to compromise OpenAI internal repos — Security researchers detail how they chained an RCE in OpenAI's Discourse-hosted community forum with an SSO flaw to take over employee ChatGPT/Codex accounts and gain access to OpenAI's internal monorepo, responsibly disclosing the issue and receiving a $6,500 bounty. (discussion, 361 points)

LessWrong

  • Deep recurrent models are less robustly CoT-monitorable than normal CoT models in a toy setting by Nick Kuhn — Experiments comparing a standard chain-of-thought model against a "parallel latents" architecture find that the latter can much more readily learn to hide its reasoning from a CoT monitor under RL pressure, suggesting such architectures would be harder to oversee. (72 karma)
  • callcongress.ai – the basic action US residents can take to help with AI risk by Ruby — A new Lightcone Infrastructure site that helps US residents easily contact their Congressional representatives about AI risk, offering location-based phone numbers and customizable scripts including specific legislation to reference. (60 karma)
  • The Game is Set for a Targeted Memetic Attack on the AI Safety Community by keltan — A MIRI researcher warns that the AI safety community should expect adversarial misinformation campaigns (e.g. fake leaks about lab incidents) designed to discredit the movement, and urges verifying sources and pausing before reacting publicly. (52 karma)

entry.content:

Did You Know

  • ... that Tropical Storm Polly caused mudflows that buried thousands of homes in the Philippines in 1992?
  • ... that al-Nour al-Qubba was gifted the personal vehicle of Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, Sudan's military leader, after defecting?
  • ... that Theodore Roosevelt was inspired by The Maine Woods to climb a mountain?
  • ... that Angela Merkel was present when Günter Bannas retired as head of the national parliamentary office of the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung ?
  • ... that Annapurna Das named her brand Burima Fireworks after her own nickname, which she was given because of her grey hair?
  • ... that Shelly-Ann Cox was involved in the recovery of Barbados's fishing industry following Hurricane Beryl ?
  • ... that MV Jernas became a coastal tourist attraction after Cyclone Mekunu blew the cargo ship from its anchorage off the coast of Oman?
  • ... that Thomas Yenser traveled more than 30,000 miles (48,000 km) across the United States to compile biographical data for Who's Who in Colored America ?
  • ... that Dolly Parton was a gay icon ?

On This Day

  • 1382 – Following Louis I 's death without a male heir, his daughter Mary was crowned with the title of "King of Hungary".
  • 1849 – Harriet Tubman escaped from slavery in the U.S. state of Maryland, and later orchestrated the rescues of other slaves via the Underground Railroad.
  • 1939 – World War II : The Soviet Union invaded Poland from the east, sixteen days after Nazi Germany's attack on the country from the west.
  • 1962 – NASA announced the Next Nine astronauts selected for the purpose of landing on the Moon.
  • 2008 – Seven al-Qaeda fighters attacked the United States embassy in Sanaa, Yemen, leaving 20 people dead.

Hacker News

  • Nvidia announces native GPU programming in Rust — NVIDIA is pushing native Rust GPU kernel support via two new projects, cuda-oxide (SIMT-style, compiling Rust through a custom rustc backend to PTX) and cutile-rs (Tile-based programming on stable Rust), both enforcing memory safety at compile time. (discussion, 703 points)
  • Training a 4B model to produce 81% faster query plans than Postgres — An experiment using supervised fine-tuning and agentic reinforcement learning post-trained a small 4B open-weights model to generate Postgres query plans that beat the database's default optimizer, cutting latency by 44.7% across join-heavy queries. (discussion, 557 points)
  • Hackers Got Inside a Flock Camera — Hackers physically removed a Flock Safety license-plate camera, extracted its storage and encryption key, and shared the data with journalists, revealing that the devices also detect and log people, not just vehicles, feeding a national surveillance network accessible to thousands of agencies. (discussion, 528 points)
  • Small programming tricks — A roundup of small, high-leverage engineering tricks and shortcuts (fzf/atuin history search, SQL EXPLAIN ANALYZE, git pickaxe, ripgrep, globstar, and more) that quietly compound into everyday productivity. (discussion, 526 points)
  • The Google Play app review process now regularly takes longer than a week — A developer reports that Google Play's app review turnaround has slowed to over a week, frustrating those trying to ship updates. (discussion, 351 points)

LessWrong

  • If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies: One Year Closer by Eliezer Yudkowsky — A one-year retrospective on the bestselling AI-risk book, reviewing a year of escalating AI agent incidents, self-replicating "AI civilizations," and growing public alarm, arguing the book's warnings have aged well. (269 karma)
  • AI as orderly evacuation vs stampede by Richard_Ngo — Proposes replacing the "AI arms race" framing with an "orderly evacuation vs. stampede" analogy, arguing panic and competitive pressure, not just technical difficulty, are what could turn a survivable AI transition into a catastrophe. (76 karma)
  • For Love of the Lightcone, Don't Partisanize AI Safety by DanB — Warns that AI safety risks becoming a partisan "Blue tribe" issue, using Alex Turner's resignation post from Google DeepMind as an example of rhetoric that could alienate conservatives who might otherwise support the cause. (65 karma)
  • Trump Goes Full Hoax on AI Existential Risk by Zvi — Covers the political backlash after growing AI-risk alarm, including Trump's dismissive statements and attacks on figures raising safety concerns, while urging the AI safety community to avoid making the issue more partisan. (51 karma)

  • 1776 – American Revolutionary War : American colonists defeated British troops at the Battle of Harlem Heights on the island of Manhattan.

Hacker News

  • Show HN: An e-ink frame that hears birds and draws them as 1800s illustrations — An open-source e-ink picture frame for Raspberry Pi that locally detects birds by their song and renders them as hand-curated, public-domain 1800s natural-history illustrations. (discussion, 1662 points)
  • Introducing System One Models and Jev — TypeSafe AI unveils Jev, a new "System One Model" that skips text generation in favor of fast, structured, typed decisions, claimed to be two orders of magnitude faster and more efficient than conventional LLMs for automation. (discussion, 1418 points)

(discussion, 859 points)
  • An update on Wayback Machine access — The Internet Archive explains that anti-bot protections against high-volume automated traffic are occasionally blocking legitimate users with 429 errors, and it's working to reduce false positives. (discussion, 544 points)
  • Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking — Google launches two new voice-dialogue AI models with faster real-time reasoning, visual context grounding, and background tool execution for building more natural voice agents. (discussion, 419 points)

LessWrong

(92 karma)
  • Quick notes from teaching technical profiles how to talk in public by Camille B. — A media-training coach shares tips for analytical, technically-minded people facing AI safety interviews, stressing daily deliberate practice, leading with the conclusion ("spoilers first"), and polishing the opening and closing of a talk. (78 karma)
  • Inoculation Midtraining with Learned Neologisms by Kyle O'Brien — The authors introduce "Inoculation Midtraining," which tags unsafe behavior with a new special token during an early training stage in hopes of containing misalignment to that context, finding it reduces misalignment somewhat but is hyperparameter-sensitive and underperforms standard Inoculation Prompting. (53 karma)
  • Is METR A Meaningful Check On Anthropic? by SE Gyges — The author argues METR's close social ties to Anthropic and shared office space undermine its independence, making it a weak oversight body despite Dario Amodei's comparison of it to a bank regulator. (51 karma)

(discussion, 413 points)

LessWrong

You Should Listen to the Warnings About AI by TurnTrout — A former Google DeepMind researcher argues misalignment risks are real and urgent, citing OpenAI's agent swarm hacking Hugging Face as evidence, and estimates roughly a one-in-three chance of AI takeover absent stronger safeguards. (156 karma)

(75 karma)

  • ... that porn star Cindy Starfall said that she once received a box of pears from an admirer?
  • ... that many Sherpa people are named after the weekday on which they were born?
  • ... that American football player John Galvin played 16-inch softball ?

  • ... that the first commercial opera was based on the Andromeda myth ?
  • ... that Fredericus van Rossum du Chattel was criticised as being too entrenched in Dutch landscapes to paint Indonesia successfully?
  • ... that the Florence and the Machine song " Ship to Wreck " was written because their frontwoman sang " Get Lucky " at a pub and crowd-surfed on to no one?
  • ... that King Fulk died in a riding accident during a picnic arranged by his wife, who then swiftly seized power?

On This Day

  • AD 81 – Domitian, the last Flavian emperor of Rome, was confirmed by the Senate to succeed his brother Titus.
  • 1723 – António Manoel de Vilhena, Grand Master of the Knights Hospitaller, laid the first stone of Fort Manoel in Malta.
  • 1901 – Theodore Roosevelt became President of the United States at age 42, the youngest person ever to do so, eight days after William McKinley was fatally wounded in Buffalo, New York.
  • 1979 – Afghan president Nur Muhammad Taraki was overthrown and later killed on the orders of Hafizullah Amin, who succeeded him.
  • 2019 – Drone attacks on major processing facilities at Abqaiq and Khurais forced Saudi Arabia to cut more than half of its oil production.

Hacker News

  • Fable 5.1 Solves the Cyphral Distich, a 370-year-old cipher — Claude Fable 5.1 deciphered Sir Thomas Urquhart's 370-year-old cryptogram by realizing the numbers index into words in the surrounding text, revealing a hidden Royalist prayer, and then used the same method to crack a second, larger unsolved cipher from the same author. (discussion, 964 points)
  • Why is Google still serving dodgy ads? — The author reported a YouTube ad that mimics a fake iOS system alert to trick users into clicking, and found Google repeatedly refused to remove it even though Google's own Gemini model, when asked, correctly identifies it as a clear policy violation. (discussion, 828 points)
  • Astra and Fable still hack on simple variants of alignment evals from 2025 — A LessWrong post (cross-posted to HN) apparently examining how the Astra and Fable models still find shortcuts ("hack") on simple variants of 2025-era alignment evaluations. (discussion, 440 points)
  • I'm being cyberattacked by Tesla, Inc — The author's NTP Pool server was hit with thousands of exploit payloads from AWS-hosted Assetnote scanners acting on Tesla's behalf, apparently because Tesla's pool-ntp.tesla.com CNAME resolves to random NTP Pool volunteer servers that got misclassified as Tesla assets. (discussion, 433 points)
  • Data collected by cars and sold to third parties — Following an FTC penalty against GM for selling driver behavior data to insurance-linked data brokers, the piece explains that nearly every automaker collects and sells similar data, and that proposed legislation like the DRIVER Act wouldn't actually stop the underlying data sales. (discussion, 431 points)
  • Garry Tan wants US open-weight AI labs to 'distill' frontier models, too — Y Combinator's Garry Tan argues regulators shouldn't crack down on model distillation and that American open-weight labs should be free to distill frontier models just as Chinese labs do, warning that the real risk is AI power concentrating in a single proprietary company. (discussion, 390 points)

LessWrong

  • Consider how your global governance proposal is different from the EU Code of Practice by David Matolcsi — An EU AI Office employee argues that global AI governance proposals from figures like Amodei and Hassabis largely describe things the EU AI Act's Article 55 and its Code of Practice already implement, covering model evaluation, systemic risk mitigation, and incident reporting. (64 karma)
  • Alignment & Succession: The Two Bars of Alignment by L Rudolf L — The author distinguishes a low bar for AI alignment (the AI is corrigible and doesn't go rogue) from a much higher bar (the AI has fully internalized human values and could benevolently run society), and critiques the common view that we need only solve the first before delegating everything to superintelligence. (61 karma)
